findings.desc: doc-code-drift: CLAUDE.md §"Open Questions (OQ) 通道 (B-ed3e)" (line 626) still says the scope-plan reviewer reads the `<requirementsDir>/decisions/` 全目录 (FULL directory) unconditionally. This diff replaces that unconditional full-scan behavior in packages/main/templates/agents/lattice-review-scope-plan.md (and its .claude/.lattice-codex mirrors) with a bounded candidateSpecSet-first routing contract (memory/playbook preflight -> filename enumeration -> candidateSpecSet build, max 15 full-reads -> scanEscalationReason-gated full scan). CLAUDE.md has zero mentions of candidateSpecSet, scanEscalationReason, or the search budget contract anywhere in the file, so it documents the old always-full-scan behavior as still current.
findings.resolvedReason: CLAUDE.md:626 OQ-channel paragraph rewritten to the bounded search-budget contract wording (commit 1dec06106); verified fixed by docs lane round-2 pass RP-004 and concept lane RP-003.

findings.desc: doc-code-drift: packages/main/templates/agents/lattice-review-behavior.md line 163 claims its candidateSpecSet inputs are consumed through the "same bounded channel as lattice-review-scope-plan", but the two prompts define different candidateSpecSet source lists. scope-plan (line 124): checklist relatedDocs; story title/description/keywords/riskSignals; changed files and symbols; command/config names; `lattice aux_doc_list` output; and top-N rg keyword matches. behavior (line 130): checklist relatedDocs, story title/description/keywords/riskSignals, changed files/symbols, command/config names, and top-N rg keyword matches -- `lattice aux_doc_list` output is omitted. Same discrepancy is mirrored identically in .claude/agents/lattice-review-behavior.md and .lattice-codex/agents/lattice-review-behavior.md (byte-identical to the template). Either behavior silently drops an input source scope-plan uses (breaking the claimed shared-channel guarantee) or the "same bounded channel" wording is inaccurate.
findings.resolvedReason: lattice aux_doc_list added to behavior candidateSpecSet source list (commit 1dec06106), restoring parity with scope-plan; verified item-by-item by docs lane RP-004 (table) and concept lane RP-003.

findings.desc: reviewer-scan-budget-guard-smoke.ts:63-65 lineIsEscalationPath() exempts any line containing the bare substring "scanEscalationReason" from all banned-pattern checks, regardless of whether the mention actually conditions/gates the scan on that line. A future prompt edit could combine an unconditional full-scan instruction with an unrelated scanEscalationReason mention on the same line (e.g. "Always scan the full decisions/ directory; ignore scanEscalationReason.") and the guard would silently pass it (verified: this hostile line matches bannedUnconditionalRules["always scan full decisions"] but is exempted before the rule loop runs). All current prompt usages are legitimately gated today, and the same substring-exemption idiom is already used by the sibling retired-authority-vocabulary-guard-smoke.ts (lineIsQuarantined), so this is an accepted line-granularity tradeoff rather than a novel defect -- flagging as low severity so a tighter same-clause check (e.g. requiring only-with/unless adjacency to scanEscalationReason) can be considered if this guard is hardened later.

CHK-002:adversarial:0 verificationEvidence command 'rg -n "advisory only" -e "gateEvidence=false" -e "NEVER satisfy" packages/main/templates/agents/lattice-review-scope-plan.md packages/main/templates/agents/lattice-review-behavior.md' is not genuinely re-runnable as bound: once any -e flag is present, ripgrep treats the bare positional "advisory only" as a PATH argument, not a search pattern (ripgrep 14.1.1 semantics). Replaying the literal command exits 2 with 'rg: advisory only: No such file or directory (os error 2)', not 0/pass as recorded -- the first pattern is silently never searched and the command errors rather than succeeding. It still prints matches for the other two -e patterns before erroring, which is why it can look like a pass on casual inspection, but exit code and true coverage do not match the recorded result=pass. Fix: move all three patterns behind -e (e.g. rg -n -e "advisory only" -e "gateEvidence=false" -e "NEVER satisfy" ...) and rebind evidence with the corrected literal command.

quality-cleanup (F-003 follow-up, residual): reviewer-scan-budget-guard-smoke.ts:65-66 escalationConditioningPattern branch `only with(?: a| an)? [^.;]*scanEscalationReason` is a proximity/keyword match, not a semantic conditioning check, so it can still be satisfied by a hostile line that pairs an unconditional full-scan instruction with a scanEscalationReason mention that does not actually gate the scan on the same clause. Verified bypasses (all return lineIsEscalationPath=true, i.e. wrongly exempted from bannedUnconditionalRules): (1) "Always scan the full decisions/ directory only with scanEscalationReason lying around unused."; (2) "Always scan the full decisions/ directory with a recorded scanEscalationReason of \"N/A\"."; (3) "Always scan the full decisions/ directory; only with a scanEscalationReason value, which can be empty.". All six current prompt-copy lines remain correctly exempted (verified) and the round-1 hostile line ("...ignore scanEscalationReason.") is now correctly flagged (verified) -- F-003 itself is fixed. This is a lower-bar residual: the guard cannot parse true semantic conditioning (e.g. an if/only-when clause actually governing the verb), so any hostile edit that keeps the literal words \"only with ... scanEscalationReason\" near an unconditional-scan sentence still slips through undetected. Low severity per round-1 bar; worth a follow-up if this guard is hardened again (e.g. require the conditioning phrase to be the clause immediately governing the banned verb, not merely present anywhere on the line).
